shared_quantity_search.continuous_p_tau217: Not shared. P-1403 reports continuous plasma p-tau217 only as ROC AUC (0.75 alone, Figure 3B; text range 0.74-0.81 across plasma, CSF and PET tau) and gives no continuous hazard ratio. P-1421 reports continuous serum p-tau217 only as restricted-cubic-spline HRs against its own median. For NC to MCI the curve is roughly flat (point estimate about 1.4 at z = +2, upper bound about 2.3, read from Figure 1), and there is no AUC. The metric types differ.
shared_quantity_search.single_marker_dichotomy: P-1421 only: p-tau217 above vs below 0.134 pg/mL (serum, ALZpath Simoa), HR 1.07 (0.73-1.56) basic, 1.19 (0.75-1.88) fully adjusted. P-1403 reports no T+ vs T- or whole-sample p-tau217 hazard ratio; its Cox models are by joint A/T group against A-T- only.
shared_quantity_search.nearest_marker_contrast: P-1403 A-T+ vs A-T- (7 vs 127 participants), HR 4.25 (1.60-11.31): a p-tau217-positive vs negative contrast restricted to plasma-amyloid-normal participants, on a threshold 2 SD above the Abeta-PET-negative mean. Its interval misses P-1421's basic interval by 0.04 (1.60 vs 1.56) but overlaps the fully adjusted one (0.75-1.88). The comparison also differs, because P-1421's contrast does not condition on amyloid and cuts at a dementia-optimised threshold.
shared_quantity_search.joint_A_T: P-1403 only (A+T+ 7.81, 3.92-15.59). P-1421 has no A/T classification.
shared_quantity_search.amyloid: Both null with overlapping intervals (P-1403 A+T- vs A-T- 1.14, 0.58-2.24; P-1421 Abeta42/40 low vs high 0.98, 0.72-1.34): no disagreement.
shared_quantity_search.crude_proportions: Not a common quantity. P-1403's counts give 21/28 (75%) progression among plasma T+ vs 39/187 (21%) among T- (derived from p.5). P-1421 gives NC-to-MCI transitions per participant, 81/803 (10%) high vs 230/1345 (17%) low, a count that includes repeat transitions after reversion and the 381 participants with MCI at baseline, and it cannot be interpreted without the age time scale.

strongest_case_against_the_verdict: The two papers ask the same question about the same marker in the same kind of person with the same metric: does elevated baseline blood p-tau217 in cognitively unimpaired older adults raise the hazard of incident MCI? P-1403 says yes, in its title. Its effect sits entirely on the tau dimension (A+T+ 7.81, 3.92-15.59; A-T+ 4.25, 1.60-11.31; A+T- 1.14, 0.58-2.24), and the authors state that amyloid did not improve the predictive value of the tau markers, so the joint A/T contrast is in substance a p-tau217 contrast. P-1421 says no, for p-tau217 as a dichotomy (1.07, 0.73-1.56; adjusted 1.19, 0.75-1.88), as a continuous spline and in marker combinations. Both of P-1403's tau-positive intervals exclude P-1421's basic interval, and the A+T+ interval excludes the adjusted one as well. Task (T2, normal cognition to MCI), modality family (blood biomarkers) and validation tier (n/a) match. The dataset-family mismatch is what independent replication looks like and could be waived, as the cohort difference in C-232 was. Cut-point differences are a matter of degree: a continuous null across P-1421's whole range leaves no threshold at which a hazard ratio of 4 to 8 could appear.
why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: The case fails because neither paper reports an estimate on a quantity the other reports, and the differences that separate the nearest pair are differences of estimand, not of gate. (1) Continuous p-tau217 is an AUC in P-1403 (plasma p-tau217 alone 0.75, Figure 3B) and a spline HR against the median in P-1421, which reports no AUC. (2) P-1403 never reports T+ vs T-. Its nearest contrast, A-T+ vs A-T-, conditions on normal amyloid and rests on 7 exposed participants, and its separation from P-1421 holds only against the basic model (lower bound 1.60 vs upper bound 1.56); it disappears against the adjusted 0.75-1.88. (3) The cut-points define different contrasts. P-1403's T+ sits 2 SD above the mean of Abeta-PET-negative CU adults (13% of its sample; specificity 97%, sensitivity 34% for progression), chosen 'to optimize the detection of AD pathology'. P-1421's cut is the Youden optimum for 10-year all-cause dementia, with 37% of the sample 'high'. From Table 1's quartiles (Q3 0.12 pg/mL under age 78), fewer than 321 of the 1,283 participants under 78 can be above 0.134 pg/mL, so at least 483 of the 803 'high' participants (60% or more) are aged 78 or over, whereas PREVENT-AD's plasma sample averages 65 years. Neither paper places P-1403's 3.98 pg/mL plasma threshold on P-1421's serum z-axis, so the spline cannot be read at P-1403's threshold; the 'continuous null' argument therefore does not reach P-1403's contrast. (4) The endpoint differs in construct. P-1403's MCI is a consensus diagnosis requiring a complaint and/or decline over multiple annual follow-ups, judged on all time points. P-1421's is a per-visit psychometric state (1.5 SD below the age-specific mean in one domain) with reversion modelled, assessed every six years under age 78; its NC-to-MCI hazard is a reversible transition intensity, and the authors note that such deficits are not necessarily the expression of an underlying neuropathology. (5) P-1403 scopes its claim ('Future studies in diverse populations and community settings are needed'), so a community null answers a question P-1403 left open rather than refuting its result. A dataset-family waiver would be reasonable, and the verdict should not rest on the gate; but a waiver cannot supply a shared exposure scale or a shared endpoint (the C-232/C-80 reasoning). No corpus study bridges the pair on a comparable quantity: P-1346 studies memory-clinic MCI to AD, and P-1289 studies amyloid and MCI due to AD in SCD. I checked all 25 first-reader quotes on their cited pages (all verbatim, four after joining a line-break hyphen) and every number in their file against the PDFs, and found no factual error. Figure 3 now supplies the plasma-specific AUCs that record_defect 2 said the text omits: 0.75 for p-tau217 alone and 0.77 combined with Abeta42/40.
grounds: No shared continuous estimate exists: P-1403 gives continuous plasma p-tau217 only as a ROC AUC (0.75 alone, Figure 3B), and P-1421 gives continuous serum p-tau217 only as spline HRs against its median, so the metric types differ.
No shared dichotomous estimate exists: P-1403's Cox models are by joint A/T group against A-T-, and it reports no T+ vs T- or whole-sample p-tau217 hazard ratio.

The nearest pairing, A-T+ vs A-T- (4.25, 1.60-11.31; 7 vs 127 participants), conditions on normal plasma amyloid, which P-1421's contrast does not, and its interval overlaps P-1421's fully adjusted 0.75-1.88.

The thresholds differ by construction: P-1403's T+ (2 SD above the Abeta-PET-negative mean; 13% positive; 97% specificity) targets AD pathology, while P-1421's cut (Youden for 10-year all-cause dementia; 37% high) targets dementia, and at least 60% of P-1421's high group is aged 78 or over (derived from Table 1 quartiles).

The endpoint differs in construct: P-1403 counts persistent consensus MCI with a complaint and/or observed decline on annual assessments, while P-1421 models a reversible per-visit psychometric state assessed every three or six years.

Horizon and model differ: P-1403 fits a Cox model from plasma sampling over a mean 5.65 years, while P-1421 fits a Gompertz multistate Markov intensity on an age time scale over a mean 9.6 years (up to 16).

The population behind the label differs (family-history-enriched CU adults, mean age 65 and 41% APOE e4, vs a random community sample with median age 72 and 40% aged 78 or over), and P-1403 itself names community settings as untested.
The dataset-family mismatch could reasonably be waived, but a waiver cannot cure the exposure and endpoint differences (C-232 and C-80 reasoning), so the verdict does not depend on the gate.
On amyloid, the only other overlapping arm, both papers are null with overlapping intervals (1.14, 0.58-2.24 vs 0.98, 0.72-1.34), so there is no second site of disagreement.
